headline: A new University of Maryland, Baltimore County poll finds that more than three-quarters of Maryland likely voters oppose new data centers.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: a clear public-opinion result released 8 Oct 2026, from one poll with a 3.5-point margin of error.
importance_line: Maryland voters of every group measured say no to new data centers, which raises pressure on candidates in the governor's race, but this is one poll of 776 likely voters.
summary: The Baltimore Banner reports that a UMBC Institute of Politics poll of 776 likely voters, taken 22 to 27 Sep with a 3.5-point margin of error, found only 13% support new data centers in the state and 16% support them near their own communities, with opposition across party, age and income groups. Governor Wes Moore, who once promoted data centers, has proposed review standards and a task force but not a pause, while rivals in the governor's race call for a moratorium or a ban.
